questions.question_text: What is the value of the $3$rd entry (entry index $r = 2$) of Row $8$ of Pascal's triangle?

options.why: Evaluated $^{8}C_{3}$ using index $3$ instead of the $0$-indexed entry $r = 2$.
Used Row $7$ instead of Row $8$, evaluating $^{7}C_{2} = 21$.
Used entry index $r = 1$ instead of $r = 2$.

questions.question_text: In the expansion of $(x+y)^{9}$, what is the coefficient of $x^{6}y^{3}$?

options.why: Evaluated $^{9}C_{2} = 36$ using the wrong power exponent.
Subtracted exponents to use index $6-3=3$ incorrectly on a different row.
Used the power of $x$ as the top index, evaluating $^{6}C_{3} = 20$.

questions.solution_text:
The coefficient of $x^{n-r}y^{r}$ in $(x+y)^{n}$ is $^{n}C_{r}$.
Here $n = 9$ and $r = 3$:
$^{9}C_{3} = \dfrac{9 \times 8 \times 7}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 84$.

options.why: Added the lower indices $4 + 5 = 9$ instead of taking the greater index $5$.
Kept $n = 11$ and added the lower indices.
Added both the upper and lower indices together.

questions.question_text: What is the sum of all entries in Row $7$ of Pascal's triangle?

options.why: Calculated $2^{6} = 64$ using Row $6$ instead of Row $7$.
Calculated $2^{8} = 256$ using Row $8$ instead of Row $7$.
Computed $7^{2} = 49$ instead of $2^{7} = 128$.

questions.solution_text:
The sum of all entries in Row $n$ is $\sum_{r=0}^{n} {^{n}C_{r}} = 2^{n}$:
For Row $7$: $2^{7} = 128$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate $^{3}C_{3} + {^{4}C_{3}} + {^{5}C_{3}} + {^{6}C_{3}} + {^{7}C_{3}}$ using the Hockey Stick identity.

options.why: Evaluated $^{8}C_{3} = 56$ without incrementing the lower index.
Evaluated $^{9}C_{3} = 84$ with incorrect indices.
Only evaluated the last term $^{7}C_{3} = 35$ instead of summing all terms.

questions.solution_text:
By the Hockey Stick identity $\sum_{k=r}^{n} {^{k}C_{r}} = {^{n+1}C_{r+1}}$:
Here $r = 3$ and $n = 7$:
$\sum_{k=3}^{7} {^{k}C_{3}} = {^{8}C_{4}} = \dfrac{8 \times 7 \times 6 \times 5}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 70$.

questions.question_text: Given $^{16}C_{3k-2} = {^{16}C_{k+6}}$ where $3k-2 \ne k+6$, find the value of $k$.

options.why: Equated $3k - 2 = k + 6 \implies k = 4$, which violates the given condition $3k - 2 \ne k + 6$.
Substituted into $(3k-2) + (k+6) = 12$ instead of the upper index $16$.
Arithmetic error: solved $4k + 4 = 16$ as $4k = 20$.

questions.solution_text:
By the symmetry property $^{n}C_{a} = {^{n}C_{b}}$ with $a \ne b$, $a + b = n$:
$(3k - 2) + (k + 6) = 16$
$4k + 4 = 16$
$4k = 12$
$k = 3$.

questions.question_text: Evaluate $^{10}C_{3} + 2{^{10}C_{4}} + {^{10}C_{5}}$ by reducing to a single combination.
questions.solution_text:
Group the terms using Pascal's addition rule:
$({^{10}C_{3}} + {^{10}C_{4}}) + ({^{10}C_{4}} + {^{10}C_{5}})$
$= {^{11}C_{4}} + {^{11}C_{5}}$
$= {^{12}C_{5}}$
$= \dfrac{12 \times 11 \times 10 \times 9 \times 8}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 792$.
